title: Phenobarbital — maintenance dosing and levels (AES summary)

maintenance.doseText: Adults and children ≥13 y: initial 60 mg/day or 1–4 mg/kg/day; maintenance 1–4 mg/kg/day; adult maximum 240 mg daily
notes: Per-kg doses kept as text: the source doesn't state which weight to use
No current FDA-approved adult label; AES took phenobarbital data from an older PI (1997 PDR)

renalNotes: 25–50% excreted unchanged by the kidneys; no renal dose rule in source
Elimination ↑ by diuretics, alkaline urine and activated charcoal
hepatic: Do not use in hepatic encephalopathy or marked hepatic impairment
ivPo: Forms: tablets, elixir 4 mg/mL, IV solution; oral bioavailability ~95%; source gives no IV ↔ PO conversion
enteral: Tube administration not addressed in source — confirm with pharmacy
levels: 15–45 mcg/mL — AES 2024 summary Table 1 (range from AES Treatments Committee clinical experience, not the label)
interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inducer: ↑ metabolism of phenytoin, lamotrigine, oral contraceptives, warfarin, corticosteroids and many other drugs (AES Table 1)
Valproate ↓ phenobarbital elimination; MAOIs prolong its effects (AES Table 1)
Synergistic CNS and respiratory depression with alcohol and sedatives; caution with pain medications and CNS depressants (AES Table 1)
Cenobamate ↑ phenobarbital — consider reducing phenobarbital (Xcopri Table 5)
Phenobarbital ↓ oxcarbazepine MHD 25–49% (Trileptal §7.2), ↓ carbamazepine (Tegretol Precautions), shortens zonisamide half-life (Zonegran Clinical Pharmacology)
pearls: Taper very slowly after chronic use — barbiturate withdrawal can cause convulsions and delirium and may be fatal (AES Table 1)
Do not use in porphyria or marked respiratory disease (AES Table 1)
Can cause respiratory depression, hypoventilation, bradycardia and hypotension (AES Table 1)
sources: Vossler DG, Gidal BE; American Epilepsy Society Treatments Committee. A Summary of Antiseizure Medications Available in the United States, 4th edition. American Epilepsy Society; revised April 1, 2024 (user-supplied)
Xcopri (cenobamate) tablets US prescribing information. SK Life Science; revised 8/2025 (user-supplied label)
Trileptal (oxcarbazepine) film-coated tablets and oral suspension US prescribing information. Novartis; revised 10/2026 (user-supplied label)
Tegretol (carbamazepine) tablets and suspension; Tegretol-XR extended-release tablets US prescribing information. Novartis; revised 8/2026 (user-supplied label)
Zonegran (zonisamide) capsules US prescribing information. Advanz Pharma; revised 9/2026 (user-supplied label)
